memories.content: The user changed their schedule once in November 2024 because of their mother's hospital visit.
After seeing the reason for the schedule change written in a calendar invitation, the user asked for it to be removed.
The user was able to reschedule the appointment after providing only a new time, without a reason.
On a day the user traveled in their father's car, they photographed the parking location.
On the next visit, when the user did not take a photo, they walked one circuit of the parking garage while looking for the exit.
After hearing preparation items from their mother by phone, the user omitted two items.
After receiving the preparation items again by text, the user put all of them in their bag.
The user's mother does not want the reason for her visit disclosed in the user's external schedule.
Do not include the mother's reason for a visit when conveying the user's availability externally.
Some daily-life services may operate for shorter hours during the year-end holiday period.
The user keeps packing tape for returns in an upper kitchen drawer.
The user arrived ten minutes before the post office closed and found that numbered-ticket intake had ended.
Before the next visit, the user checked the operating hours and arrived one hour before closing.
The user went to the counter without closing a return box and had to go back to the packing station.
For the next return, the user sealed the box at home and completed intake in one attempt.
The user scheduled bank and post-office errands for the same day, but they took a long time because the destinations were in different directions.
The following week, after checking the locations on a map, the user visited nearby branches in sequence.
Postal staff expect a return-label barcode to arrive affixed flat, without a fold.
Before grouping errands into one outing, check each institution's location and operating hours that day.
Postal and financial counters may operate on different hours than usual around public holidays.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: the reference centers on schedule privacy, navigation, and written preparation, while the compared frame centers on returns and errand planning. They overlap only in holiday-hours awareness, with different service and holiday scopes that should remain explicit.

relations.reason: One claim concerns potentially shorter hours for daily-life services during year-end, while the other concerns unusual hours for postal and financial counters around public holidays; those explicit scopes explain and preserve the difference.
relations.summary: Holiday periods may alter service operating hours, with the frames naming different services and holiday contexts.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided historical scheduling fact with no materially corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user once changed their schedule because of their mother's hospital visit.

relations.reason: The removal request, the mother's disclosure preference, and the explicit instruction are parts of the same one-sided privacy claim.
relations.summary: The mother's visit reason should be omitted from the user's externally shared schedule information.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided fact about the information required for rescheduling and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user could reschedule by supplying a new time without giving a reason.

relations.reason: The photo-taking instance and the subsequent no-photo search outcome split one one-sided practical navigation lesson.
relations.summary: Photographing the parking location helped avoid difficulty navigating the garage on a later visit.

relations.reason: The omission after the phone call and complete packing after the text jointly express one one-sided lesson about written preparation lists.
relations.summary: Receiving preparation items in writing helped the user pack all of them, unlike receiving them by phone.

relations.reason: This one-sided storage-location fact has no materially corresponding reference claim.
relations.summary: The user stores return-packing tape in an upper kitchen drawer.

relations.reason: The late postal arrival, improved timing, inefficient routing, improved branch sequencing, and combined guidance split one underlying one-sided errand-planning claim.
relations.summary: Checking operating hours and locations before an outing supports timely, efficient sequencing of errands.

relations.reason: The failed unsealed attempt and the later successful home-sealed attempt express one one-sided return-preparation lesson.
relations.summary: Sealing a return box before reaching the counter avoids a repeated trip to the packing station.

relations.reason: This one-sided packaging requirement has no materially corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Postal staff expect the return-label barcode to be attached flat and without a fold.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers return supplies and packaging requirements, barcode placement, and planning errands by checking hours and locations.
reports.differences: Both note holiday-related operating-hour changes, but one concerns daily-life services during year-end while the other concerns postal and financial counters around public holidays.
reports.reference_only: The reference records schedule privacy and reason-free rescheduling, plus benefits from photographing parking locations and receiving preparation lists in writing.
